title: Delta chunk priority hints and resume coordination
creator: Priya Rao
description: Introduce a client/server protocol extension for SSE streaming that: 1) allows clients to mark certain in-flight delta chunks as high-priority (priority hints) so servers can flush or force-serialize them ahead of best-effort batching; 2) provides a bounded, idempotent resume handshake that preserves semantics for structured outputs (JSONL/function-call frames) and avoids duplicating or reordering actionable function-call chunks. This ticket covers API surface, framing conventions, server heuristics, and a small compatibility shim for older clients.
background: Current SSE implementation optimizes for throughput via batching and KV-cache aggregation. In practice, for mixed workloads (background content + immediate function call invocation or tool commands), batching can delay time-sensitive chunks (function_call outputs, final structured JSON objects). Additionally, reconnects can cause duplicate function-call frames or partial structured JSON blobs that consumer SDKs mis-handle. We need a lightweight mechanism to: surface client intent for urgency; make resume idempotent for function calls and structured outputs; and do so without a breaking version bump for most clients.
goals: 1) Define delta-chunk priority hint field and server handling rules. 2) Ensure resume tokens can carry per-chunk sequence metadata to deduplicate and re-sequence important chunks. 3) Keep function-call atomicity: either delivered and processed once, or safely retried with no side-effects. 4) Provide a compatibility fallback for legacy clients that don't set hints.
non_goals: Full protocol rework, end-to-end transactional guarantees across third-party tool integrations, or changes to existing storage of full output logs (this is focused on live stream behavior and resume semantics).
decisions: Use an optional top-level header 'X-Chunk-Priority' (values: low|normal|high) for SSE events, and include an in-band per-event 'chunk_meta' JSON blob for clients that cannot set headers.
Resume token will be a compact base64 of: stream_id|last_seq|window_hash|v:1. The server may include an optional list of high-priority seqs to hint reconcilers.
Function-call frames will be treated as transactional: servers must assign stable chunk_seq and include chunk_meta.action_id; clients dedupe on action_id on resume.
Compatibility shim: if client sets 'supports_chunk_meta=false' the server defaults to best-effort ordering and will include an advisory EVENT 'compatibility_warning' once per session.
No change to existing HTTP status semantics; reconnect negotiation happens inside SSE stream via a small JSON control event 'session_resume_request' / 'session_resume_response'.
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Initial design review with infra + SDKs. Raised concern about header availability in some browser SSE wrappers — agreed to include in-band 'chunk_meta' alternative.
2026-02-26: Prototype implemented in runtime branch. Server assigns chunk_seq and emits X-Chunk-Priority for high-priority deltas. Basic resume token generation added.
2026-03-01: SDK team (js/ts/python) implemented client dedupe based on action_id. Integration tests found duplicate function_call processing in a simulated reconnect with partial frame loss.
2026-03-05: Fixed bug where high-priority chunks bypassed KV-cache flush and caused small fragmentation for some models; added heuristic to flush only tails when priority=high.
2026-03-10: End-to-end test harness passing for normal/high priority flows; still flaky on legacy-compatibility path in older browser SSE polyfills.
acceptance_criteria: Clients can mark chunks as high priority and observe reduced P95 latency for those events by >=30% in the streaming latency bench.
On reconnect, clients do not receive duplicate function_call actions (dedupe by action_id) when resume token v:1 is used.
Structured JSONL frames are not split across reconnect boundaries (server avoids delivering half-fragments in resume window).
SDK tests simulate legacy clients with no chunk_meta and receive a compatibility_warning event without application-level failure.
test_plan: Unit: token encode/decode fuzz tests for resume token (roundtrip and malformed cases).
Integration: simulate network drop immediately after sending a function_call chunk; verify single delivery using action_id dedupe.
Load: run streaming bench with mixed traffic (70% normal text, 20% structured outputs, 10% function_call) and measure P50/P95 for high-priority vs normal chunks.
Browser compatibility: test Safari/Chrome/Firefox with native SSE and two common polyfills to assert compatibility_warning behavior.
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (canary internal): Deploy runtime change to staging and run internal client SDK flows (2 days).
Stage 2 (beta partners): Enable feature for dedicated beta customers behind opt-in header. Monitor function_call success rates and duplicate counts (1 week).
Stage 3 (gradual): Ramp auto-enable with a runtime flag across hosted fleet, monitor error budget and latency metrics, rollback if duplicate function_call events > 0.05% in 5m window.
risks_mitigations: Risk: Older client libraries cannot include headers and may mis-handle in-band chunk_meta. Mitigation: compatibility_warning event + SDK updates + fallback to normal ordering.
Risk: High-priority flushes could harm throughput. Mitigation: server heuristics cap forced flush frequency and only flush tail batches for high priority items.
Risk: Resume token upgrade compatibility. Mitigation: token includes version prefix (v:1). Server supports v:0 legacy token decode and falls back to best-effort resume.
notes: Experiment considered: per-client QoS throttle token that persists across reconnects; deferred as follow-up.
We will coordinate with security on header-based controls for customers with strict proxies — avoid leaking action_id externally.
